forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Vale of White Horse investment returns ahead of budget as deposit rates beat forecast
news_drafts.lead: The Vale of White Horse council expects to receive £1.146m more in investment income than budgeted for 2026–27, driven by higher returns on its treasury deposits, the cabinet heard this week. The council's cash reserves are earning 4.26 per cent on average, outperforming the government's Sterling Overnight Index Average benchmark of 3.74 per cent. However, the council is also forecasting a £698,000 overspend on employee costs in the first quarter, largely because of spending on staff for the local government reorganisation programme, project surveyors and temporary legal cover. A £0.7m underspend on disabled facilities grants, which fund home adaptations for disabled people, is under national review by the Department for Health and Social Care, and the council risks having to return unspent money.

findings.paper_title: Appx 1 Progress against the IA plan 2025-26 - Copy
findings.headline: Three audits deferred from 2025/26 plan - two due to ongoing Ocella replacement project, one prioritized to 2027/28
findings.detail: Three audits were deferred from the 2025/26 plan. The CIL Income and Ocella Replacement audits were deferred pending completion of the ongoing Ocella replacement project, while Supplier Relationship Management was moved to the 2027/28 audit plan. These deferrals create temporary gaps in audit coverage of these control areas.
findings.matters: Audit deferrals create coverage gaps during the deferral period, reducing the scope of independent assurance over these functions until work resumes.
findings.figures: 3 audits deferred (2 pending Ocella project completion, 1 to 2027/28 plan)
findings.quote: Work on Ocella replacement continues, priority for IA once project is completed.

findings.paper_title: Appx 1 Progress against the IA plan 2025-26 - Copy
findings.headline: All eight key financial control audits completed with Substantial assurance - 5 management actions identified, all Priority 3
findings.detail: Eight Key Financial audits covering Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable, Council Tax, General Ledger, NNDR, Treasury Management, Payroll, and Housing Benefit Claims and Council Tax Reduction Scheme all achieved Substantial assurance ratings. Combined, these audits identified only 5 management actions, all classified as Priority 3 (minor findings). No Priority 1 or 2 findings were identified in any core financial control.
findings.matters: Substantial assurance ratings across all core financial controls indicate the fundamental financial control environment is operating effectively, supporting confidence in financial stewardship and external audit reliance.
findings.figures: 8 audits completed with Substantial assurance; 5 total management actions (all Priority 3); 0 Priority 1; 0 Priority 2
findings.quote: Treasury Management Key Financial Q3 & Q4 Completed Substantial 0 - - -

findings.paper_title: Appx 1 Progress against the IA plan 2025-26 - Copy
findings.headline: Cyber Security audit completed with Limited assurance rating - 9 management actions including 2 Priority 1 findings
findings.detail: The cyber security audit (including AI considerations) was completed in Q4 with a Limited assurance rating, indicating control weaknesses in this critical area. Nine management actions were identified to address findings, including two Priority 1 items requiring immediate attention.
findings.matters: Weaknesses in cyber security controls affect the integrity and security of financial systems and data, which underpins financial governance and external audit reliance.
findings.figures: Limited assurance, 9 management actions (2 Priority 1, 5 Priority 2, 2 Priority 3)
findings.quote: Cyber Security (incl. AI) Audit Q4 Completed Limited 9 2 5 2

findings.headline: Eight Priority 1 audit actions remain overdue as of 25 September 2026.
findings.detail: Eight Priority 1 actions (defined as fundamental to service business processes requiring immediate management attention) are past their scheduled completion dates. These relate to site visit audits (Cornerstone, Beacon, Abbey House) and housing landlord audits from 2025/26, affecting Development & Corporate Landlord and Communities services. Overall, 67 of the 131 open audit actions are past due.
findings.matters: Overdue Priority 1 actions indicate management has not implemented fundamental control recommendations as required within their target timescales. This increases operational and financial risk, particularly given that fundamental control weaknesses across multiple services remain unresolved.
findings.figures: 8 past due Priority 1 actions; 67 past due of 131 total open actions
findings.quote: the 8 past due, priority 1 actions as of 25th September 2026, relate to the following audits:

findings.headline: Cyber security audit received Limited assurance with 9 management actions including 2 Priority 1.
findings.detail: Audit of cyber security (including AI) for 2025/26 received Limited assurance, indicating significant gaps and weaknesses requiring improvement. The audit raised 9 management actions: 2 Priority 1 (fundamental to service integrity), 5 Priority 2 (important), and 2 Priority 3. Limited assurance means significant improvement is required to the control environment to effectively manage risks.
findings.matters: Cyber security controls are fundamental to protecting council data, maintaining service continuity, and meeting regulatory obligations. Control weaknesses in this area create operational and information security risk across all council functions.
findings.figures: Limited assurance rating; 9 management actions (2 Priority 1, 5 Priority 2, 2 Priority 3)

daily_post.headline: Disabled Facilities Grant underspend of £0.7m under national department review, with risk of clawback
daily_post.lead: A national review of DFG underspends raises the risk of clawback or reduced future allocations, which could constrain the council's ability to support disabled residents' adaptations and may signal funding pressure across the sector.
